vibe.rationale: Vibe 3 — lower edge, held. June 8 morning opens at 3, unchanged from June 7 evening's lower-edge close. The Sunday signing window passage without a confirmed deal is the defining overnight event: it does not collapse the deal framework (gap narrowing reporting persists, Iran comms channel intact, no formal rejection issued), but it eliminates the deal-confirmation upside catalyst that was available entering June 7. The architecture remains delay-not-collapse at Day 3, but each day without a response compresses the credibility of that framing and incrementally raises the probability that the counter-demand cycle enters multi-week stall territory. Four conditions sustain Vibe 3 this morning: (1) Iran comms resolved Day 5 — private channel structurally open, no re-suspension signal in the Sunday-to-Monday overnight; (2) US-Iran gap characterization from June 7 evening remains the operative framing — narrowing, not widening; (3) Ghalibaf Day 3 without retraction or ultimatum escalation — the public-private bifurcation preserved; (4) Beirut-suburbs partial truce Day 6 overnight clean — Lebanon track stable, no Israeli scope creep into Dahiyeh or Hezbollah cross-border action. Three conditions prevent morning upgrade to 4: (1) no Iranian substantive response to the counter-demand has materialized as of morning — Day 3 silence presses 'delay not collapse' credibility; (2) Mojtaba Khamenei's non-approval of the MOU text persists as the structural bottleneck unchanged; (3) Ghalibaf Day 3 unretracted — public hardline posture continues as the dominant visible Iranian face. Upgrade to 4 requires: confirmed Iranian substantive response to the counter-demand; Beirut truce Day 7 clean. Upgrade to 5 requires: MOU signing confirmed with Hormuz transfer timeline operative. Drop to 2 requires: formal Iranian rejection of amendment counter-demand; Ghalibaf or Khamenei escalation to ultimatum tier; CENTCOM repositioning signal; Lebanon partial truce collapse.

items.summary: Four secondary infrastructure threads entering June 8. First: the NSF Newport OR ocean observatory removal is advancing toward end-of-June completion (WA coastal stations removed September 2025). The permanent loss of this monitoring network degrades: atmospheric river early detection, real-time ocean temperature for marine heat wave and fisheries forecasting, wave height and storm surge data for coastal emergency management, and Pacific maritime monitoring. This degradation is structural and permanent absent a federal policy reversal. The NOAA severe geomagnetic storm warning today illustrates the operational sensitivity of the loss — a functioning ocean buoy network would normally provide enhanced space-weather-impact monitoring for marine surfaces now being eliminated. Second: T-HUD full committee markup at $92.224B (-10.4% from FY26) has not advanced to House floor scheduling. Sound Transit's $34.5B funding gap remains the primary regional transit capital risk. Sound Transit Link Light Rail is the primary transit mode for Lumen Field FIFA access beginning June 15 — T-HUD federal match risk is directly operationally relevant to the co-response planning window now live. Third: nationally, battery storage deployment is accelerating — installations tracking significantly above the 2025 full-year record, with BESS providing growing grid backstop function. However, the 224 GW AI data center incremental load forecast through 2035 continues outpacing battery storage and transmission modernization capacity; large transformer lead times remain at two years; grid queue backlogs exceed 2,500 GW of stalled projects. Fourth: Sound Transit World Cup operational preparedness is fully active — trains every eight minutes on 1 Line and 2 Line on all match days, four-minute headways in the downtown core, service extended to 1 a.m.

analyst_summary: June 8, 2026 morning opens at Vibe 3 — lower edge, held. The Sunday signing window has passed without a confirmed Iran MOU amendment signing, and June 8 morning opens Counter-Demand Day 3 with no Iranian substantive response as of morning. The 'delay not collapse' framing holds: Iran comms are resolved (Day 5, no re-suspension), the US-Iran gap is characterized as narrowing from June 7 evening reporting, Ghalibaf is at Day 3 without retraction or ultimatum, Beirut suburbs partial truce holds at Day 6 overnight clean, and CENTCOM has no kinetic resumption signal. But each additional day of counter-demand silence compresses the credibility of that framing — Monday is the first opportunity for Tehran to break the silence with a substantive signal, and the day's single most important watch item is whether it does. Two positive overnight developments: Armenia parliamentary results project Pashinyan Civil Contract for a strong majority (South Caucasus second-order risk reduction confirmed), and Peru early ONPE counts show Fujimori leading (Andean critical minerals supply chain continuity in view). Domestically, WPA crosses the triple-digit milestone at Day 100 (Day 10 past the hard constitutional deadline) without enforcement or litigation. DHS/ICE reconciliation enters the House floor action window today. Reconciliation 2.0 is T-26 days to the July 4 deadline with no floor date confirmed. Warsh Day 25 silent with FOMC T-8 and CPI arriving Wednesday — the June 10 CPI print is the next market-moving domestic catalyst regardless of Iran outcome. Infrastructure: NIFC-FIFA co-response window is NOW LIVE at T-3; NOAA's severe geomagnetic storm warning introduces a cross-domain stress vector for BPA transmission, wildfire air operations GPS, and HF radio. Longview CSB advances to Day 14 unresolved. NSF ocean observatory removal off Newport OR advancing toward end-of-June completion. Morning's watch architecture has one primary question: Iran — does Day 3 Monday produce a substantive signal from Tehran? Secondary: does the FOMC T-8 + CPI Wednesday risk window tighten with additional inflation signal before Warsh breaks his silence?
